verdicts.evidence: On Gaussian/exponential kernels in 2D/3D/5D (n=80–120), the Sinkhorn construction yields row-sum errors ~1e-13 and mass-weighted self-adjointness relative errors ~1e-16; breaking kernel symmetry or using row normalization raises the error to 1e-2–1e-1, confirming the property is discriminating.

Sup-norm errors of T_N f − T_ref f decrease monotonically with clean algebraic rates (1D: ~2nd order; 2D: ~1st–1.3rd order) across N=32→256 (1D) and 10²→32² (2D) for both Gaussian and exponential kernels on bounded domains; the sign-oscillating kernel mutation causes divergence, confirming positivity is load-bearing.

Across 40 configurations (dim 2/3, two kernel families, five bandwidths, uniform/non-uniform mass, n=200), iteration counts to reach 1e-3 relative error are min 6, median 9.5, max 11, with 90% landing in the 5–10 window; the extreme-mass-range mutation needing 14 iterations is honestly reported as a boundary case.

The Sinkhorn operator scores 4/4 properties (symmetry ~1e-16, mass ~1e-12, positivity, spectrum [0,1]) for prescribed non-uniform mass, but row normalization evaluated against its own degree measure also satisfies all four (sym err 2.2e-16, mass err 4.4e-16, spectrum [5.4e-4, 1.0]), a genuine counter-example to the exclusivity sub-clause.

All three data types (point cloud n=900, sparse voxel shell n=773, GMM n=300) show Dirichlet-energy decay, monotone damping, and constant-annihilation, but the jaw-bone voxel scan is replaced by a synthetic 24³ hollow shell proxy, so the paper's actual assets are not used.

Cross-modality group-mean eigenvalue deviations on a unit-sphere proxy (n=900, three sampling modalities) are 1.9–3.1% and grow with mode index, qualitatively matching the claim, but the Armadillo mesh is unavailable and the sphere is a synthetic stand-in.

overall: The logbook provides concrete, mutation-tested numerical evidence supporting the two theorems (Claims 1–2) and the empirical iteration-count claim (Claim 3), while honestly surfacing a counter-example to Claim 4's exclusivity sub-clause. Claims 5–6 are addressed only on synthetic proxy geometries (sphere, synthetic shell) rather than the paper's actual jaw-bone and Armadillo assets, limiting them to toy-level reproductions of qualitative behavior.
